purpose: offline expected behavior generated by executing selected immutable Windows Python AST definitions; no network or native tools
stubs: PassiveSourceClient.get_json is replaced by a scripted Client returning fixture JSON or a scripted 404 exception; URL, params, cache_key and retry-status arguments are recorded.
Orchestrator provider result functions are inert callables; _provider_plan itself is executed and its registered keys are observed.
resolve_host is executed for DNS cases with query_rr replaced by scripted RRQuery responses; actual query order is captured.

WildcardAnalyzer.analyze_parent executes its source implementation with resolve_host replaced by ordinal-scripted HostResolution results carrying RRQuery A signatures; secrets.token_hex and datetime.now are fixed for deterministic labels/timestamps.
Provider iter_jsonl reads only a generated local temporary JSONL file; inventory/rank/serialization source definitions execute unchanged.

Source Event/EventType/ScopeStatus AST definitions execute with deterministic timestamp/UUID providers; DNS _emit_resolution_records/_validation_event and passive _health_event execute unchanged while append_event and DNSRunIndex are minimal capture sinks that preserve fields. ScopeChecker always returns in_scope for these authorized fixture names. _health_event scenarios use actual ProviderObservation/ProviderResult AST dataclasses with scripted result values. Event IDs and timestamps are omitted from outputs.
Domain normalization is a minimal ASCII-only stand-in; full PSL and Unicode normalization are covered by phase1 fixtures.

evidence.completeness AST constants, AnomalyAssessment, classify_completeness, detect_provider_output_anomaly, unique_contribution_by_provider and build_run_artifact execute unchanged with stdlib statistics and scripted ProviderResult/provenance/history; no filesystem history discovery occurs. Artifact historical rows are context only. The legacy academic_purpose field is preserved as a source compatibility key that describes user-result trust, not academic metrics.
